analysis.title: NY Open - Slippery
key_insights: Risk sentiment is soft. US tech weakness is still weighing on stocks, and geopolitical catalysts are ahead. KOSPI was the worst Asian performer at -3.5% overnight.

The dollar is holding its highs near key levels: USDJPY 160 (resistance) and EURUSD 1.0950-1.1000 (support). Citi's view is that dovish Fed pushback and geopolitics will matter more for the dollar than AI concerns.

The Citi vol desk sees consistent EUR downside interest across tenors and expressions. The FX eTrading desk saw net buying of EUR from investor and leveraged names on interbank volumes 15% below the 30-day average.

Heavy Fedspeak starts today: Williams at 09:05 ET (FX market structure conference, unlikely to cover rates), Chair Warsh at midday (not clear he will address policy), Hammack at 14:15 on Bloomberg. Citi Economics expects no comments on the near-term path of policy this week.
Citi Economics sees consecutive 25bp hikes in Dec and Jan as more likely than a 50bp move next month. Waller has put a 50bp December hike on the table.
USTs are in wait-and-see mode. The desk saw slightly better paying flow overnight through the belly of the curve.

Gilt yields are higher into a pivotal UK data week. BoE hike expectations have been reinforced by data, and this week's CPI and labor report could add support. Citi sees limited immediate market implications from the Brexit headlines (PM Burnham calling for a new deal).

NQA contracts are -1% into the cash open, with US tech sentiment low. NVDA is -2.3% premarket after last week's CEO resignation. The FT reports Jensen Huang is discussing a possible comeback, and Bessent said a 'dramatic' leadership shake-up is needed. ES1 losses are more modest, and airlines are heavy after Friday's grounding.

A Citi salesperson sees investor focus shifting from 'AI road builders' (semis, hardware) to 'AI toll operators' that monetize AI. Beneficiaries named are hyperscalers (Google of interest), enterprise software/cyber, fintech and biotech.

China October real economy data was broad-based weak. Retail sales slowed to 0.4% YoY on payback effects and industrial production softened, which suggests downside risk to Citi's 2026 China GDP forecast. Iron ore is under selling pressure.
Crude is flat awaiting geopolitical developments. A Putin/Xi/Trump meeting is confirmed for Thursday. Iran targeted a Bahrain air defense base overnight but suggested a path to a US deal is open.

Week ahead: APEC in Shenzhen on Nov 18-19 (US-China trade, chip restrictions, Taiwan, Russia-Ukraine, Iran), Nvidia earnings Tuesday, FOMC minutes, 20 Fedspeak events, UK jobs and inflation data that decide whether the MPC hikes in Dec, Japan GDP/CPI, Canada CPI, Australian wages and employment, and China activity data.

Canada CPI (08:30 ET): Citi Economics expects headline to accelerate to 0.4% MoM against consensus of 0.3% and 0.1% prior. With inflation trends soft, Citi's house view is that the BoC holds in the near term.

Poland core CPI (08:00 ET): Citi Economics estimates a decline to 2.8% from 3.1% based on the partial breakdown of the flash release. That implies little spillover from high commodity prices to consumer prices.
Israel CPI undershot at 1.1% YY. ILS is looking through the miss amid geopolitics and a weaker shekel. The print leaves the door open for a cut next week but not more.

BRL: Bloomberg reported Lula's government plans fiscal measures that could add BRL20bn to the adjustment. Flows were muted last week, and the theme is approaching seasonal year-end outflows rather than acute repositioning by real money.
earnings_insights: Nvidia earnings (Tuesday): Citi's weekly preview says they 'should beat' (expectation, no EPS or revenue figures given), though questions about leadership should persist.
Major US and China retail earnings and tech earnings are scheduled this week, with no figures or estimates given.
